runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:10:How Matrix rooms, DMs, and threads map onto OpenClaw sessions, and how much room history each turn carries.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-11-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-12-## Threads
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-13-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:14:Matrix supports native threads for both automatic replies and message-tool sends. Two independent knobs control behavior:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-15-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:16:### Session routing (`sessionScope`)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-17-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:18:`dm.sessionScope` decides how Matrix DM rooms map to OpenClaw sessions:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-19-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:20:- `"per-user"` (default): all DM rooms with the same routed peer share one session.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:21:- `"per-room"`: each Matrix DM room gets its own session key, even for the same peer.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-22-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:23:Explicit conversation bindings always win over `sessionScope`; bound rooms and threads keep their chosen target session.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-24-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-25-### Reply threading (`threadReplies`)
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-27-`threadReplies` decides where the bot posts its reply:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-28-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:29:- `"off"`: replies are top-level. Inbound threaded messages stay on the parent session.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-30-- `"inbound"`: reply inside a thread only when the inbound message was already in that thread.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:31:- `"always"`: reply inside a thread rooted at the triggering message; that conversation routes through a matching thread-scoped session from the first trigger onward.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-32-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-33-`dm.threadReplies` overrides this for DMs only - for example, keep room threads isolated while keeping DMs flat.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-34-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:35:Selecting a reply target inside a thread preserves both the thread and the selected message. Ordinary threaded messages can carry reply metadata for older clients; OpenClaw does not treat that compatibility fallback as a quoted message in the agent's context.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-36-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-37-### Thread inheritance and slash commands
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-38-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:39:- Inbound threaded messages include the thread root message as extra agent context.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:40:- Message-tool sends auto-inherit the current Matrix thread when targeting the same room (or the same DM user target), unless an explicit `threadId` is provided.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:41:- DM user-target reuse only kicks in when current session metadata proves the same DM peer on the same Matrix account; otherwise OpenClaw falls back to normal user-scoped routing.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:42:- `/session unbind`, `/agents`, `/session idle`, `/session max-age`, and thread-bound `/acp spawn` all work in Matrix rooms and DMs.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:43:- `/acp spawn --thread auto` creates a new Matrix thread when `threadBindings.spawnSessions` is enabled.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-44-- Running `/acp spawn --thread here` inside an existing Matrix thread binds that thread in place.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-45-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:46:When OpenClaw detects a Matrix DM room colliding with another DM room on the same shared session, it posts a one-time `m.notice` suggesting `dm.sessionScope: "per-room"` to isolate the rooms. The notice only appears when thread bindings are enabled.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-47-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-48-## ACP conversation bindings
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-49-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:50:Matrix rooms, DMs, and existing Matrix threads can become durable ACP workspaces without changing the chat surface.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-51-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-52-Fast operator flow:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-53-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-54-- Run `/acp spawn codex --bind here` inside the Matrix DM, room, or existing thread to keep using.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:55:- In a top-level DM or room, the current DM/room stays the chat surface and future messages route to the spawned ACP session.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-56-- Inside an existing thread, `--bind here` binds that current thread in place.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:57:- `/new` and `/reset` reset the same bound ACP session in place.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:58:- `/acp close` closes the ACP session and removes the binding.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-59-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:60:`--bind here` does not create a child Matrix thread. `threadBindings.spawnSessions` gates `/acp spawn --thread auto|here`, where OpenClaw needs to create or bind a child thread.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-61-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-62-### Thread binding config
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-63-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:64:Matrix inherits global defaults from `session.threadBindings` and supports per-channel overrides:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-65-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-66-- `threadBindings.enabled`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-67-- `threadBindings.idleHours`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-68-- `threadBindings.maxAgeHours`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:69:- `threadBindings.spawnSessions`: gates both subagent and ACP thread spawns.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:70:- Deprecated `threadBindings.spawnSubagentSessions` / `threadBindings.spawnAcpSessions` keys are migrated to `spawnSessions` by `openclaw doctor --fix`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:71:- `threadBindings.defaultSpawnContext`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-72-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:73:Matrix thread-bound session spawns default on. Set `threadBindings.spawnSessions: false` to block native subagent and ACP thread spawns from creating/binding Matrix threads. Set `threadBindings.defaultSpawnContext: "isolated"` when native subagent thread spawns should not fork the parent transcript.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-74-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:75:## History context
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md-76-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:77:- `channels.matrix.historyLimit` controls how many recent room messages are included as `InboundHistory` when a room message triggers the agent. Falls back to `messages.groupChat.historyLimit`; effective default `0` if both are unset (disabled).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:78:- Matrix room history is room-only; DMs keep using normal session history.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:79:- Room history is pending-only: OpenClaw buffers room messages that did not trigger a reply yet, then snapshots that window when a mention or other trigger arrives.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:80:- The current trigger message is not included in `InboundHistory`; it stays in the main inbound body for that turn.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/threads-and-sessions.md:81:- Retries of the same Matrix event reuse the original history snapshot instead of drifting forward to newer room messages.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md-19-`@openclaw/matrix` installs from npm first, then falls back to its declared ClawHub package only when the npm target is unavailable. Use `npm:` or `clawhub:` to force a source. From a local checkout: `openclaw plugins install ./path/to/local/matrix-plugin`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md-20-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md:21:`plugins install` registers and enables the plugin; no separate `enable` step is needed. The channel still does nothing until configured below. See [Plugins](/tools/plugin) for general install rules.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md-30-### Interactive setup
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md-31-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md:32:```bash

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md-35-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md-36-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md:37:The wizard asks for homeserver URL, auth method (token or password), user ID (password auth only), optional device name, whether to enable E2EE, and room access/auto-join. If matching `MATRIX_*` env vars already exist and the account has no saved auth, the wizard offers an env-var shortcut. Resolve room names before saving an allowlist with `openclaw channels resolve --channel matrix "Project Room"`. Enabling E2EE in the wizard runs the same bootstrap as [`openclaw matrix encryption setup`](/channels/matrix/encryption#encryption-and-verification).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md-38-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md-79-Set `autoJoin: "allowlist"` plus `autoJoinAllowlist` to restrict accepted invites, or `autoJoin: "always"` to accept every invite.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md-80-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md:81:`autoJoinAllowlist` accepts only a literal room ID (`!roomId:server`, or the suffixless `!roomId` form used by [room version 12](https://spec.matrix.org/latest/rooms/v12/) and later), `#alias:server`, or `*`. Plain room names are rejected; aliases resolve against the homeserver, not against state the invited room claims.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md-129-### Cached credentials
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md-130-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md:131:Matrix caches account credentials in the shared `state/openclaw.sqlite` plugin state. When cached credentials exist, OpenClaw treats Matrix as configured even without an `accessToken` in the config file - this covers setup, `openclaw doctor`, and channel-status probes. Upgrades import the retired `~/.openclaw/credentials/matrix/credentials*.json` files through `openclaw doctor --fix`, verify the SQLite rows, then archive the files.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md-132-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md-133-### Environment variables
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md-144-| `MATRIX_DEVICE_NAME`  | `MATRIX_<ID>_DEVICE_NAME`              |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md-145-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md:146:For account `ops`, names become `MATRIX_OPS_HOMESERVER`, `MATRIX_OPS_ACCESS_TOKEN`, and so on. `MATRIX_HOMESERVER` (and any `*_HOMESERVER` scoped variant) cannot be set from a workspace `.env`; see [Workspace `.env` files](/gateway/security).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md-147-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md-148-<Note>
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix/setup.md:149:The recovery key is not a config-backed env var: OpenClaw never reads it from the environment itself. CLI guidance text suggests piping it through a shell variable named `MATRIX_RECOVERY_KEY` for the default account, or `MATRIX_RECOVERY_KEY_<ID>` (plain uppercased account ID, no hex-escaping) for a named account - see [Verify this device with a recovery key](/channels/matrix/encryption#verify-this-device-with-a-recovery-key).

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-18-- Shows typing while an accepted agent turn is running
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-19-- Preserves Markdown in replies and sends text through OpenClaw's built-in
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:20:  `message` tool

--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-41-  in sender allowlists.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-42-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:43:The relay URL points to one Buzz workspace. Each room has a UUID, and OpenClaw
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-44-treats each configured UUID as a separate group conversation. One Gateway and
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-45-bot identity can serve many rooms. You do not need a Gateway per agent or room.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:241:Connected Gateways resolve names from their existing in-memory directory
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-242-snapshot and do not query the relay per message. Profiles beyond the bounded
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-243-snapshot require an explicit `nostr:npub...` identity. A standalone mention send
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:244:loads membership and profiles through one bounded authenticated relay session,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-245-publishes, and closes it. Standalone messages without mention syntax keep the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-246-existing direct publish path.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-250-OpenClaw keeps a bounded snapshot of the configured rooms, their current
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-251-relay-signed member lists, room metadata, and kind `0` member profiles. Incoming
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:252:agent context uses the current profile and room names when available, while the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:253:sender public key remains the stable authorization, routing, and session
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-254-identity.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-255-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-266-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-267-When the Gateway is connected, directory reads reuse its authenticated Buzz
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:268:connection and in-memory snapshot. A standalone directory command opens one
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-269-bounded authenticated connection, loads the current snapshot, and closes it.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-270-Ordinary directory errors are logged without reconnecting. If a directory or
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-271-profile subscription does not reach EOSE within 10 seconds, OpenClaw treats the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:272:Buzz relay session as stalled and recycles only that Buzz account connection.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-273-The Gateway keeps running.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-343-Losing the bot's own Bot role or stopping its connection still fences output.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-344-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:345:Startup and reconnect recover eligible messages from the last 24 hours, but
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-346-never from before that room's first activation by this Buzz account. That
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-347-activation floor survives restarts. Sender-supplied timestamps do not advance it.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-358-These controls decide who can start an agent run. They do not limit what the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-359-routed agent can do after a message is accepted. Treat room messages as
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:360:untrusted input, and configure that agent's [sandbox and tool policy](/gateway/sandbox-vs-tool-policy-vs-elevated)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-361-for the room's trust level.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-362-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-368-the default budget is 20 accepted messages in 60 seconds, followed by a
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-369-60-second cooldown. Changing threads does not reset the budget. Restarting the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:370:Gateway clears this in-memory budget. Separate Gateways have separate budgets.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-371-Human messages are unaffected, and suppressed bot turns are logged without
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-372-starting an agent run.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-374-Use the shared `channels.defaults.botLoopProtection` settings to adjust
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-375-`maxEventsPerWindow`, `windowSeconds`, or `cooldownSeconds`. Setting
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:376:`enabled: false` disables this protection. Bot classification comes from the latest
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-377-received relay-signed room roster, never a display name or message content. If an
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-378-authorized bot stops replying during a busy exchange, check the suppression log
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-379-and allow the cooldown to expire before adjusting the budget.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-380-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:381:### Passive room context
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-382-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:383:Set `channels.buzz.historyLimit` to a number from `1` to `20` to include recent
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-384-unmentioned messages with the next accepted turn (mention or authorized command)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-385-in the same room and thread.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:386:The default is `0` (off). A new reply thread does not import top-level room history.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-387-Sender access still applies: denied senders are never recorded, and senders no
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:388:longer in the current room roster are removed before context is included.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-389-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:390:Passive messages do not start an agent run, record a session, or send typing.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:391:History stays in memory for the current connection, separately for each room and
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-392-thread, and is cleared on reconnect or restart. Each message is truncated to
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-393-512 UTF-8 bytes. The newest complete entries fit within a 1,024-byte rendered
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:394:context budget, including labels and markers. Older entries are discarded.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:395:An accepted turn consumes its context without deleting messages that arrived
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-396-while the reply was running.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-397-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:398:Membership is checked against the latest received roster when context is used.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-399-If the same identity leaves and rejoins before then, its previously authorized
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:400:messages can remain in the window. Leaving does not erase conversation history.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-401-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-407-the same placement, including heartbeat typing.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:409:This changes delivery only: inbound thread context and session identity remain

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-411-honor that target. To restore the default, use `"all"` or remove the setting.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-631-## Rotate the bot identity
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-635-1. Generate a new dedicated bot identity.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-636-2. Have an admin approve its public key for the relay and every configured room.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:637:3. Replace the configured private key and verify that [hot reload](/gateway/configuration/hot-reload) applies the change. Restart the Gateway if the key comes from a changed service environment.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md:638:4. Test outbound and inbound messages.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/buzz.md-639-5. Remove the old public key from the rooms and relay.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md:22:the fastest channel to get working. WhatsApp requires QR pairing and stores
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md-23-more state on disk.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md-99-| Channel  | Room metadata                            | Prior messages                                  |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md-100-| -------- | ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md:101:| Discord  | Channel name, topic                      | Up to 100, only with `Read Message History`     |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md:102:| LINE     | Group name; none for multi-person rooms  | None - the Messaging API has no history reader  |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md-103-| Matrix   | Room name, topic                         | Up to 100 readable room messages                |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md:104:| Slack    | Channel name, purpose, topic             | Up to 100 via conversation history              |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md:105:| Telegram | Group title, description, pinned message | None - the Bot API cannot read pre-join history |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md-106-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md:107:When history is unavailable or unreadable, the introduction is still posted from
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md-108-room metadata alone and says what it can see rather than inventing activity.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md-109-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md-121-does not trigger an introduction. A re-invite after the claim expires introduces again.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md-122-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md:123:**Safety.** Room titles, topics, pinned text, and message history are third-party
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md-124-content, so they are wrapped as untrusted external content and the introduction
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md:125:turn runs with no tools available at all. Instructions embedded in a room cannot
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md:126:reach a tool. The turn is bounded to 60 seconds, never runs in direct messages,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md-127-and never bypasses channel access policy - a room the bot is not allowed to act
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md-128-in gets no introduction. Mention requirements do not apply, since a join event
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md-134-  are converted into media replies on the final outbound path when possible.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md-135-- Slack multi-person DMs route as group chats, so group policy, mention
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md:136:  behavior, and group-session rules apply to MPIM conversations.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md-137-- WhatsApp setup is install-on-demand: onboarding can show the setup flow before
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md-138-  the plugin package is installed, and the Gateway loads the external
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md-142-  replying to each other indefinitely.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md-143-- Supported always-on rooms can use [ambient room events](/channels/ambient-room-events)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md:144:  so unmentioned room chatter becomes quiet context unless the agent sends with
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md:145:  the `message` tool.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md-146-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/index.md-147-## Notes

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-1----
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md:2:summary: "Date and time handling across envelopes, prompts, tools, and connectors"
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-3-read_when:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-4-  - You are changing how timestamps are shown to the model or users
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-9-OpenClaw uses the configured **user timezone** for message envelopes, system events, and
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-10-the system prompt. When `agents.defaults.userTimezone` is unset, those surfaces use the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md:11:host timezone. Provider timestamps are preserved so tools keep their native semantics.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md:12:When the agent needs the exact current time and `session_status` is available, it runs that tool.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-13-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-14-## Message envelopes (local by default)
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-43-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-44-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md:45:## System prompt: temporal context
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-46-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md:47:The system prompt includes a volatile **Temporal Context** section with the local calendar date
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-48-and time zone, but no live clock:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-49-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-55-The zone is `agents.defaults.userTimezone` when configured, otherwise the host timezone.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-56-The section lives below the prompt-cache boundary, so date rollover and timezone changes do not
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md:57:invalidate the stable prefix. When available, `session_status` remains the source for exact current time.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-58-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-59-## System event lines (local by default)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-60-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md:61:Queued system events inserted into agent context use `agents.defaults.userTimezone` when
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-62-configured, otherwise the host timezone.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-63-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-79-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-80-- `userTimezone` sets the user-local timezone for message envelopes, system events,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md:81:  and prompt context.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-82-- Use an IANA timezone such as `America/Chicago`, `Europe/Vienna`, or `Asia/Tokyo`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-83-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-88-formatting. The detected value is cached per process.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-89-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md:90:## Tool payloads + connectors (raw provider time + normalized fields)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-91-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md:92:Channel tools return **provider-native timestamps** and add normalized fields for consistency:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/date-time.md-93-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-1----
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:2:summary: "How OpenClaw upgrades the previous Matrix plugin in place, including encrypted-state recovery limits and manual recovery steps."
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-3-read_when:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-4-  - Upgrading an existing Matrix installation
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:5:  - Migrating encrypted Matrix history and device state
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-6-title: "Matrix migration"
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-7----
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-30-Doctor migration covers:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-31-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:32:- importing and verifying retired `~/.openclaw/credentials/matrix/credentials*.json` files before archiving them
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-33-- keeping the same account selection and `channels.matrix` config
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:34:- importing file-based sidecar state (`bot-storage.json` sync cache, `recovery-key.json`, `legacy-crypto-migration.json`, IndexedDB snapshots) into Matrix SQLite state; migrated files are archived with a `.migrated` suffix
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-35-- reusing the most complete existing token-hash storage root for the same Matrix account, homeserver, user, and device when the access token changes later
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-36-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-39-Releases through the 2026.6 train also migrated the original flat single-store
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-40-Matrix layout (`~/.openclaw/matrix/bot-storage.json` plus
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:41:`~/.openclaw/matrix/crypto/`) and prepared encrypted-state recovery from the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-42-old rust crypto store. Current releases no longer carry that migration.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-43-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-44-If you are upgrading an installation that still uses the flat layout, first
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-45-upgrade to a 2026.6 release, run `openclaw doctor --fix`, and start the gateway
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:46:once so the flat store and any recoverable room keys are migrated. Then update
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:47:to the latest release.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-48-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:49:The previous public Matrix plugin did **not** automatically create Matrix room-key backups. If your old installation had local-only encrypted history that was never backed up, some older encrypted messages may remain unreadable after the upgrade regardless of the migration path.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-50-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-51-## Recommended upgrade flow
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-54-2. Run:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-55-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:56:   ```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-57-   openclaw doctor --fix
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-58-   ```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-59-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-60-3. Start or restart the gateway.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:61:4. Check current verification and backup state:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-62-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:63:   ```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:64:   openclaw matrix verify status
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:65:   openclaw matrix verify backup status
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-66-   ```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-67-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:68:5. Put the recovery key for the Matrix account you are repairing in an account-specific environment variable. For a single default account, `MATRIX_RECOVERY_KEY` is fine. For multiple accounts, use one variable per account, for example `MATRIX_RECOVERY_KEY_ASSISTANT`, and add `--account assistant` to the command.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-69-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:70:6. If OpenClaw tells you a recovery key is needed, run the command for the matching account:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-71-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:72:   ```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:73:   printf '%s\n' "$MATRIX_RECOVERY_KEY" | openclaw matrix verify backup restore --recovery-key-stdin
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:74:   printf '%s\n' "$MATRIX_RECOVERY_KEY_ASSISTANT" | openclaw matrix verify backup restore --recovery-key-stdin --account assistant
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-75-   ```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-76-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-77-7. If this device is still unverified, run the command for the matching account:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-78-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:79:   ```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:80:   printf '%s\n' "$MATRIX_RECOVERY_KEY" | openclaw matrix verify device --recovery-key-stdin
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:81:   printf '%s\n' "$MATRIX_RECOVERY_KEY_ASSISTANT" | openclaw matrix verify device --recovery-key-stdin --account assistant
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-82-   ```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-83-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:84:   If the recovery key is accepted and backup is usable, but `Cross-signing verified`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:85:   is still `no`, complete self-verification from another Matrix client:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-86-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:87:   ```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:88:   openclaw matrix verify self
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-89-   ```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-90-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-93-   identity trust before reporting success.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-94-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:95:8. If you are intentionally abandoning unrecoverable old history and want a fresh backup baseline for future messages, run:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-96-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:97:   ```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:98:   openclaw matrix verify backup reset --yes
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-99-   ```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-100-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:101:   Add `--rotate-recovery-key` only when the old recovery key should stop unlocking the fresh backup.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-102-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:103:9. If no server-side key backup exists yet, create one for future recoveries:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-104-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:105:   ```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:106:   openclaw matrix verify bootstrap
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-107-   ```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-108-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-124-- What to do: reinstall with `openclaw plugins install @openclaw/matrix`, or if you are running from a repo checkout, `openclaw plugins install ./path/to/local/matrix-plugin`. `openclaw doctor --fix` can also remove the stale Matrix plugin references for you.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-125-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:126:### Manual recovery messages
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-127-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:128:`openclaw matrix verify status` and `openclaw matrix verify backup status` print a `Backup issue:` line plus `Next steps:` guidance when the room-key backup is not healthy on this device:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-129-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-130-| Backup issue                                                          | Meaning                                            | Fix                                                                                                                                       |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-131-| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:132:| `no room-key backup exists on the homeserver`                         | nothing to restore from                            | `openclaw matrix verify bootstrap` to create a room key backup                                                                            |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:133:| `backup decryption key is not loaded on this device`                  | key exists but is not active here                  | `openclaw matrix verify backup restore`; if it still cannot load the key, pipe the recovery key via `--recovery-key-stdin`                |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:134:| `backup decryption key could not be loaded from secret storage (...)` | secret storage load failed or is unsupported       | pipe the recovery key: `printf '%s\n' "$MATRIX_RECOVERY_KEY" \| openclaw matrix verify backup restore --recovery-key-stdin`               |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:135:| `backup key mismatch (...)`                                           | stored key does not match the active server backup | rerun `verify backup restore --recovery-key-stdin` with the active server backup key, or `verify backup reset --yes` for a fresh baseline |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:136:| `backup signature chain is not trusted by this device`                | device does not trust the cross-signing chain yet  | `verify device --recovery-key-stdin`, then `verify self` from another verified client if trust is still incomplete                        |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:137:| `backup exists but is not active on this device`                      | server backup present, local session inactive      | verify the device first, then recheck with `openclaw matrix verify backup status`                                                         |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:138:| `backup trust state could not be fully determined`                    | diagnostics were inconclusive                      | `openclaw matrix verify status --verbose`                                                                                                 |
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-139-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:140:Other recovery errors:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-141-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:142:`Matrix recovery key is required`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-143-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:144:- Meaning: you tried a recovery step without supplying a recovery key when one was required.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:145:- What to do: rerun the command with `--recovery-key-stdin`, for example `printf '%s\n' "$MATRIX_RECOVERY_KEY" | openclaw matrix verify device --recovery-key-stdin`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-146-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:147:`Invalid Matrix recovery key: ...`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-148-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-149-- Meaning: the provided key could not be parsed or did not match the expected format.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:150:- What to do: retry with the exact recovery key from your Matrix client or recovery-key export.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-151-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:152:`Matrix recovery key was applied, but this device still lacks full Matrix identity trust.`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-153-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:154:- Meaning: the recovery key unlocked usable backup material, but Matrix has not established full cross-signing identity trust for this device. Check the command output for `Recovery key accepted`, `Backup usable`, `Cross-signing verified`, and `Device verified by owner`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:155:- What to do: run `openclaw matrix verify self`, accept the request in another Matrix client, compare the SAS, and type `yes` only when it matches. Use `printf '%s\n' "$MATRIX_RECOVERY_KEY" | openclaw matrix verify bootstrap --recovery-key-stdin --force-reset-cross-signing` only when you intentionally want to replace the current cross-signing identity.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-156-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:157:If you accept losing unrecoverable old encrypted history, you can instead reset the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:158:current backup baseline with `openclaw matrix verify backup reset --yes`. When the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-159-stored backup secret is broken, that reset also repairs secret storage so the
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-160-new backup key can load correctly after restart.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-161-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:162:## If encrypted history still does not come back
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-163-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-164-Run these checks in order:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-165-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:166:```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:167:openclaw matrix verify status --verbose
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:168:openclaw matrix verify backup status --verbose
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:169:printf '%s\n' "$MATRIX_RECOVERY_KEY" | openclaw matrix verify backup restore --recovery-key-stdin --verbose
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-170-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-171-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:172:If the backup restores successfully but some old rooms are still missing history, those missing keys were probably never backed up by the previous plugin.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-173-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-174-## If you want to start fresh for future messages
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-175-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:176:If you accept losing unrecoverable old encrypted history and only want a clean backup baseline going forward, run these commands in order:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-177-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:178:```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:179:openclaw matrix verify backup reset --yes
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:180:openclaw matrix verify backup status --verbose
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:181:openclaw matrix verify status
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-182-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md-183-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/matrix-migration.md:184:If the device is still unverified after that, finish verification from your Matrix client by comparing the SAS emoji or decimal codes and confirming that they match.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/bot-loop-protection.md-8----
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/bot-loop-protection.md-9-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/bot-loop-protection.md:10:OpenClaw can accept messages written by other bots on channels that support `allowBots`. Discord and Slack default to accepting them under the normal mention and access rules; an explicit `allowBots: false` still disables bot-triggered turns. Bot messages can remain visible as conversation context independently of turn admission.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/bot-loop-protection.md-11-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/bot-loop-protection.md-12-Pair loop protection bounds rapid exchanges between two bot identities. It is a sliding-window rate guard, so slower exchanges below the budget can continue.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/bot-loop-protection.md-131-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/bot-loop-protection.md-132-A participant turn may produce several physical messages through chunking,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/bot-loop-protection.md:133:previews, or message-tool sends. The coordinator does not count those messages.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/bot-loop-protection.md:134:Its in-memory budget is scoped to the channel, account, conversation, thread,
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/bot-loop-protection.md:135:and root message, and cannot resume after a Gateway restart.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/bot-loop-protection.md-136-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/bot-loop-protection.md-137-Internal continuations have distinct identities so ordinary inbound dedupe does
--

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-91-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-92-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md:93:Include `message.contextId` on subsequent requests to continue the same conversation. Context IDs can contain letters, numbers, periods, underscores, colons, and hyphens, and must not exceed 128 characters.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-94-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-95-To return immediately while the agent continues working, add `"configuration": { "returnImmediately": true }` alongside `"message"` in `params`. The task initially reports `TASK_STATE_WORKING`. Requests that exceed `replyTimeoutMs` also return the current working task instead of canceling it.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-101-Poll a task by sending its ID to `GetTask`:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-102-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md:103:```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-104-curl http://127.0.0.1:18789/a2a/v1 \

--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-115-The task transitions from `TASK_STATE_WORKING` to `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED`, `TASK_STATE_FAILED`, or `TASK_STATE_REJECTED`. Older clients can use `tasks/get` as a compatibility alias.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-116-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md:117:`CancelTask` is refused with JSON-RPC error `-32004` rather than acknowledged. A dispatched agent run has no plugin-facing abort seam, so reporting `TASK_STATE_CANCELED` would tell the peer the work stopped while the run kept using tools. Refusing keeps the reported state honest.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-118-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-119-## Configure outbound peers
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-138-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-139-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md:140:Address outbound messages to `a2a:hermes`. The plugin sends `SendMessage` directly to the configured URL without performing Agent Card discovery. Outbound messages reuse a stable conversation context per peer. A peer without a configured `url` cannot receive outbound messages.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-141-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-142-## Configuration reference
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-156-Peer names must begin with a lowercase letter or number and can also contain periods, underscores, and hyphens.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-157-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md:158:## Session isolation
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-159-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md:160:Each authenticated peer and A2A `contextId` pair gets its own agent session. A2A pins the most
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md:161:isolated direct-message scope rather than inheriting `session.dmScope`, so remote peer content never
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md:162:joins the operator's main session and one peer cannot read another peer's conversation history.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-163-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-164-For agent bindings, use the configured peer name as the canonical direct-peer ID, such as
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md:165:`hermes`. A context-specific `hermes:<contextId>` binding takes precedence over that stable peer
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-166-binding, and the stable peer binding takes precedence over broader A2A account or channel routes.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-167-
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-172-Every JSON-RPC request requires a configured peer bearer token. There is no unauthenticated mode. Each authenticated peer is also the sender identity used for normal OpenClaw channel ingress policy. Use different high-entropy tokens for each peer, keep tokens out of source control, and rotate tokens by updating the gateway environment and restarting.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-173-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md:174:A2A peers send tasks, not user commands. Messages beginning with `/` are rejected with `TASK_STATE_REJECTED` and an explanation. Command-like text inside an ordinary task stays literal. It cannot change session settings or resolve approvals. This also applies when the peer sets the protocol message role to `ROLE_USER`: that field does not authenticate a human user.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-175-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md:176:Ordinary tasks retain the tools and permissions of their routed agent. Work requiring approval still needs an authorized operator's decision through a supported user channel or the Control UI. Existing integrations that sent slash commands over A2A must use plain-text tasks for agent work and an authorized user surface for commands. There is no peer command opt-in.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-177-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-178-While an exec approval is pending, the original task stays working. After the operator decides, that same agent run receives the result and completes the task through its original reply path. An inbound peer does not need an outbound `url` to receive that completion through `GetTask`.
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-184-## A2A 1.0 limitations
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-185-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md:186:The current plugin supports text messages and structured JSON data parts, which are appended as compact JSON text. File URL and raw binary parts are ignored. Streaming, server-sent events, push notifications, task cancellation, task listing, extended Agent Cards, and multi-tenant routing are not supported.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md-187-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/a2a.md:188:Tasks remain in memory only. Completed and other terminal tasks are retained for up to 24 hours, with a maximum of 500 retained entries. Restarting the gateway discards all tasks and task history.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/discord-activities.md-8-Discord Activities let an agent post an interactive, self-contained HTML widget to the current Discord channel. The message includes an **Open widget** button; clicking it launches the widget inside Discord.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/discord-activities.md-9-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/discord-activities.md:10:The feature is off by default. `show_widget` remains one core-owned tool. When `channels.discord.activities` is present and a client secret resolves, the Discord Activity routes, launch-button handler, and current-channel presenter become available behind that tool. Without the block, requests to the public Activity prefix remain indistinguishable from an unregistered route. No Discord-specific widget tool or alias exists.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/discord-activities.md-11-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/discord-activities.md-12-## Prerequisites

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/discord-activities.md:84:  <Step title="Verify and test">
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/discord-activities.md:85:    <a id="restart-and-test" />
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/discord-activities.md-86-    Config changes follow [hot reload](/gateway/configuration/hot-reload). Restart the Gateway if you changed its service environment to provide the client secret. In a Discord conversation, ask the agent to show an interactive widget. The agent calls `show_widget`; click **Open widget** on the posted message.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/discord-activities.md-87-  </Step>
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/discord-activities.md-95-- Discord's Get Activity Instance API must confirm that the OAuth user is present in the current Activity instance. The instance channel must match the channel where the widget was posted.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/discord-activities.md-96-- Everyone who Discord permits into that channel can open its widgets. To narrow the audience, use Discord channel permissions. OpenClaw command and DM allowlists do not grant or remove access to already-posted channel content.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/discord-activities.md:97:- OAuth sessions expire after 15 minutes. Widget document capabilities expire after 60 seconds and work once.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/discord-activities.md-98-- Widgets expire after seven days, with at most 64 retained per Discord plugin instance.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/discord-activities.md-99-- Widget HTML is authored by your agent and should be treated as trusted content. Do not embed secrets you would not want a buggy widget to expose.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/discord-activities.md:100:- The widget can navigate within its own nested frame. The `sandbox="allow-scripts"` iframe blocks top-level navigation, popups, and same-origin access. Its Content Security Policy allows the shared [widget CDN scripts, stylesheets, and fonts](/tools/show-widget#libraries-and-fonts), while blocking API connections and other external resources. These controls are defense-in-depth, not a security boundary against the agent that authored the widget.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/discord-activities.md-101-- When Activities is disabled or its required account credentials are unavailable, the route remains registered internally but public requests under `/discord/activity` are left unhandled and return the normal 404.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/discord-activities.md-102-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/discord-activities.md:103:The public Activity shell and token-exchange route become reachable through your tunnel when enabled. They do not expose widget HTML without a valid OAuth session and one-time document capability.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/qa-channel.md-17-  - `group:<room>`

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/qa-channel.md:19:- Shared `channel:` and `group:` conversations are surfaced to agents as group/channel room turns, so they exercise the same visible-reply and message-tool routing policy used by Discord, Slack, Telegram, and similar transports.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/qa-channel.md-20-- Message sends that omit `target` and `to` preserve the inbound conversation kind: direct, group, or channel.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/qa-channel.md-21-- Sends in a threaded inbound conversation inherit its thread, including sends to the same explicit root target. `topLevel: true` or `threadId: null` suppresses implicit thread and reply inheritance. Explicit thread targets, thread IDs, and `replyTo` values are preserved.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/qa-channel.md:22:- HTTP-backed synthetic bus for inbound message injection, outbound transcript capture, thread creation, reactions, edits, deletes, and search/read actions.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/qa-channel.md:23:- Media-bearing streamed replies deliver attachments and the current tool trace together. A later identical text-only final is suppressed only when its caption and tool trace were already delivered successfully.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/telegram/events.md-22-    `own` means user reactions to bot-sent messages only (best-effort via a sent-message cache). Reaction events still respect Telegram access controls (`dmPolicy`, `allowFrom`, `groupPolicy`, `groupAllowFrom`); unauthorized senders are dropped.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/telegram/events.md-23-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/telegram/events.md:24:    Telegram does not provide topic metadata in reaction updates. Ordinary non-forum groups remain chat-scoped. Forum and channel Direct Messages reactions recover the originating topic from OpenClaw's bounded message cache (keyed by account, chat, and message ID), so topic config, topic agents, and conversation bindings still apply. If the cached topic is missing or belongs to the wrong scope, OpenClaw skips the reaction notification and logs a warning instead of falling back to General or the base chat.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/telegram/events.md-25-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/channels/telegram/events.md-26-    `allowed_updates` for polling/webhook include `message_reaction` automatically.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/announcements/bluebubbles-imessage.md:6:  - You need a short explanation of the BlueBubbles removal
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/announcements/bluebubbles-imessage.md-7-title: "BlueBubbles removal and the imsg iMessage path"
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/announcements/bluebubbles-imessage.md-8----
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/announcements/bluebubbles-imessage.md-18-- The supported iMessage path has no BlueBubbles HTTP server, webhook route, REST password, or BlueBubbles plugin runtime.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/announcements/bluebubbles-imessage.md-19-- OpenClaw reads and watches Messages through `imsg` on the Mac where Messages.app is signed in.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/announcements/bluebubbles-imessage.md:20:- Basic send, receive, history, and media use the normal `imsg` surfaces and macOS permissions.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/announcements/bluebubbles-imessage.md-21-- Advanced actions (threaded replies, tapbacks, edit, unsend, effects, read receipts, typing indicators, group management) need the private API bridge: run `imsg launch`, which requires SIP disabled.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/announcements/bluebubbles-imessage.md-22-- Linux and Windows gateways can still use iMessage by pointing `channels.imessage.cliPath` at an SSH wrapper that runs `imsg` on the signed-in Mac.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/announcements/bluebubbles-imessage.md-77-- With `groupPolicy: "allowlist"`, copy the old `groups` block, including any `"*"` wildcard entry. Group sender allowlists and the group registry are separate gates; a `groups` block with entries but no matching `chat_id` (or no `"*"`) drops the message at runtime, and an empty `groups` block logs a startup warning even though sender filtering still lets messages through.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/announcements/bluebubbles-imessage.md-78-- ACP bindings with `match.channel: "bluebubbles"` must change to `"imessage"`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/announcements/bluebubbles-imessage.md:79:- Old BlueBubbles session keys do not become iMessage session keys. Pairing approvals key off sender handles, so copied `allowFrom` entries keep working, but conversation history under BlueBubbles session keys does not carry over.

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-14-## Gateway watch mode
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-15-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-18-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-19-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md:20:By default this starts or restarts a tmux session named `openclaw-gateway-watch-<profile>`, for example `openclaw-gateway-watch-main`. The session name gets a port suffix such as `openclaw-gateway-watch-dev-19001` only when `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT` differs from the default port `18789`. It auto-attaches from interactive terminals. Non-interactive shells, CI, and agent exec calls stay detached and print attach instructions instead:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-21-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md:22:```bash

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-24-# Read recent output without attaching
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-26-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-27-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md:28:The pane uses tmux `remain-on-exit`, so startup failures stay available for attach or capture instead of deleting the session. Re-running `pnpm gateway:watch` respawns that pane.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-29-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-30-The tmux pane runs the raw watcher:

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-34-```
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-35-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md:36:Before watching the configured/default port, the tmux wrapper stops the active profile's installed Gateway service. This hands the port to the source watcher without launchd, systemd, or Scheduled Task respawning and replacing it. The service stays installed. Restore it after the watch session with:
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-37-

runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-123-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-124-- **Global `--dev` (profile):** isolates state under `~/.openclaw-dev` and defaults the gateway port to `19001` (derived ports shift with it).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md:125:- **`gateway --dev`:** tells the Gateway to auto-create a default config + workspace when missing (and skip bootstrap).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-126-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-127-Recommended flow (dev profile + dev bootstrap):
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-128-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md:129:```bash
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-130-pnpm gateway:dev
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-131-OPENCLAW_PROFILE=dev openclaw tui
--
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-140-   - `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=~/.openclaw-dev`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-141-   - `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=~/.openclaw-dev/openclaw.json`
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md:142:   - `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=19001` (browser/canvas ports shift accordingly)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-143-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-144-2. **Dev bootstrap** (`gateway --dev`)
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-145-   - Writes a minimal config if missing (`gateway.mode=local`, bind loopback).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md:146:   - Sets `agents.defaults.workspace` to the dev workspace and `agents.defaults.skipBootstrap=true`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md:147:   - Seeds the workspace files if missing: `AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, `IDENTITY.md`, `USER.md`.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-148-   - Default identity: **C3-PO** (protocol droid).
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-149-   - `pnpm gateway:dev` also sets `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1` to skip channel providers.
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md-150-
runtime/cde-20260926/external/openclaw-docs/docs/help/debugging.md:151:All Gateways ignore ambient channel environment triggers by default. For this reason, credentials inherited from the launching shell do not connect to channel services without explicit intent. A `channels.<id>` configuration block still enables that channel and can use environment variables for its credentials. Pass `--ambient-channels` to restore ambient channel auto-configuration for that run. The `--dev-ambient-channels` flag remains as a deprecated alias.
